title: Shared feedback fits every answer
statement: A retry or hint message shown for every wrong answer must be true of every answer it can be shown for, and must not assume how another part was answered.
detail: In reading lessons, retry messages written for one expected wrong answer were shown for every miss: one opened with "Almost" for any miss, including answers nowhere near right, and another named a word the item itself accepted, so one student was told about that word while another who typed it passed. On a cloze, the feedback for one blank assumed the blank before it had been answered correctly.

evidence.quote: It is shown for every miss, including "scary" or "gloomy".
A student who typed "scared" is told about "miserable", and a student who typed "miserable" passes.
The `depend` feedback on blank 3 (*"That word is already in the gap before this one"*) assumes blank 2 was answered correctly.
true of *presence* only — a stemmed match proves the child said the word, never that they used it
correctly, so no reply may congratulate correct usage.
word-specific one that fires wrongly **names a word the child never said**.
asserts fired-word === named-word for every clause shown
and a child who read the sentence correctly is told they read it wrong.
